subject: Dedicated commit: throughput/latency measurement protocol & SLA proposal
messages:
From: Jason Miller <jason@cloudscale.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit: throughput & latency guarantees — measurement details

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week — CloudScale is very interested in a Reserved GPU pool for our inference workloads. Before we proceed to commercial terms, our platform team needs firm guarantees and an understanding of the measurement methodology you use to validate throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) and p95/p99 token latency.

Specifically:
- Can you define exactly how Redwood measures tokens/sec vs requests/sec for a committed pool (does it count logical requests or total generated tokens)?
- How do you handle KV cache warm vs cold starts in the acceptance run?
- Do you provide a standard harness (load spec) we can run in our lab that produces comparable numbers?
- If throughput misses occur during acceptance, what remediation or credits are available?

Also — if we commit 30K GPU-hours/mo for 12 months, what sort of up-front discount could we expect (we can be flexible on burst policies)?

We'd like documentation and a concise test plan that our infra team can run. Can you share the protocol and propose SLA language so procurement can start redlining?

Thanks,
Jason
Jason Miller
CTO, CloudScale
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Miller <jason@cloudscale.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit: throughput & latency guarantees — measurement details

Hi Jason — great to hear from you and glad the demo landed. Attaching our draft measurement protocol (dedicated-throughput-protocol-v1.pdf) and a sample workload spec (sample-workload-spec.json) so your infra team can validate locally. High level answers below, and I also proposed a short call for Monday to walk through the test harness.

Brief answers:
- Tokens/sec vs requests/sec: our SLA guarantees an average sustained tokens/sec per GPU pool band (measured as total tokens generated / measurement window). Requests/sec is treated as an operational secondary metric (useful for queuing/backpressure planning) and we report both. We will publish both numbers from the acceptance run.
- KV cache handling: acceptance runs have two phases: a warm-run (30 minutes of representative traffic to populate KV/prefix caches) followed by a 60-minute measurement window. Pass criteria are evaluated on the measurement window only; we log warm vs measurement performance separately for diagnostics.
- Standard harness: yes — the attached sample workload contains a seed distribution and sequence-length histogram matching the model family you saw in the demo. We also provide a containerized runner (link below) that emits both synthetic and replayed real-traffic traces.
- Misses & credits: our standard proposal is a 10% SLA credit for sustained under-delivery (measured as averaged tokens/sec falling below agreed band for longer than the dispute window). We include a 10 business day dispute window to run re-runs/cross-checks. I'll confirm exact credit math on Monday after internal alignment.

On discounts: for a 12-mo, 30K GPU-hour commit we can propose a tiered discount (details in the draft term sheet). I'll loop in our commercial and engineering leads to propose definitive numbers.

Call options: Mon 04/05 10:00am PT or 2:00pm PT?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated commit: throughput & latency guarantees — CloudScale request (CS-4821)

Team — forwarding Jason's note. Quick asks:
- We need a clean, prescriptive acceptance protocol for throughput/latency that we can send to customers (try to avoid the wordy legalese — keep it procedural). Attach the protocol draft I shared.
- Discount/commit proposal: Jason expects a clear band for 30K GPU-hours/mo x12. Ben — can you draft pricing bands/discounts and propose an initial ask?
- Marissa — we need explicit measurement commands, a test harness image, and the exact pass/fail math (tokens/sec delta threshold, p95/p99 latency SLOs, allowed burst window). Also propose an internal fallback if they fail the run (re-run rules, warm-cache remedies).

Important constraints from CloudScale: they want both tokens/sec and requests/sec numbers; they care about warm-cache baseline vs measurement window. They prefer a short dispute window but procurement expects a re-run period.

Deliver by Monday EOD so I can consolidate for the call.

Thanks — Priya
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated commit: throughput & latency guarantees — CloudScale request (CS-4821)

Priya — notes and concrete proposal below (technical acceptance checklist). I kept this procedural so we can paste into the PDF we send to CloudScale.

Acceptance run (sequence):
1) Warm phase: 30-minute ramp using their replay file or our standard seed. Purpose: populate KV caches, JIT/quant kernels warmed.
2) Stabilize: 10-minute cooldown to allow load balancer flaps to settle (not counted).
3) Measurement phase: 60-minute steady-state run at target concurrency. Metrics captured at 1s granularity.

Metrics & pass criteria:
- tokens_per_sec: measured as total model tokens emitted / measurement_window_seconds. Pass if averaged tokens_per_sec >= committed_rate * 0.98 (2% tolerance).
- requests_per_sec: reported as peak and 1-minute rolling average; not used for credit math but useful for capacity planning.
- latency_per_token_p95 and p99: measured on per-token generation latency. Pass if p95 <= 160ms and p99 <= 300ms for the agreed model/seq-length profile. Thresholds are configurable per model family.
- error_rate: <0.2% 5xx or OOM failures during measurement phase. Any persistent OOMs fail acceptance.

Burst handling:
- We allow a defined burst window (10 minutes) at 150% of committed tokens/sec for transient spikes. Sustained bursts beyond 10 minutes count against the measurement window and may reduce averaged tokens/sec.

Remediation & re-runs:
- If averaged tokens/sec misses by <=5%, customer may request one supervised re-run within 5 business days. We will run with identical seed and environment; logs and raw traces are shared.
- If miss >5%, default credit = (shortfall_percent) * (monthly commit charge) * 0.5 (one-time adjustment). Example math in attached term sheet.
- Dispute process: both sides have 10 business days to contest results and request re-runs.

Test harness & commands (summary):
- We provide a container image: redwood/throughput-harness:stable. Run: docker run --rm -e TARGET_URL=... redwood/throughput-harness:stable --seed-file=sample-workload-spec.json --duration=70m --warm=30m --metrics=prometheus
- We publish a small JMeter wrapper for request-level tests and a token-profiler script to convert model output to token counts.

Deliverables for customer: protocol PDF, sample workload, harness image, and a short checklist for env parity (GPU type, clock settings, quantization profile). Link to our runbook: https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated-acceptance (shared in drive link).

I'll attach a compact runbook snippet to the PDF. Ben — ping me with pricing bands and I'll slot them into the term sheet.

—Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Miller <jason@cloudscale.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit: throughput & latency guarantees — measurement details and proposed commercials (CS-4821)

Hi Jason — following up with a concrete proposal after internal alignment. Attached: dedicated-throughput-protocol-v1.pdf (protocol), sample-workload-spec.json (seed), and our draft term sheet (redwood-dedicated-term-sheet-commit-CS-4821.pdf). Summary below.

Technical proposal (high level):
- Committed baseline: 140k tokens/sec sustained reported over a 60-minute measurement window following a 30-minute warm-up.
- Burst allowance: 150% of baseline for up to 10 minutes per hour; sustained bursts count against measurement average.
- Latency SLOs (for agreed model/seq profile): p95 <= 160ms, p99 <= 300ms.
- Acceptance pass: averaged tokens/sec >= 98% of baseline AND error_rate <0.2% during measurement phase.
- Re-run / dispute: one supervised re-run within 5 business days if miss <=5%; automatic credit calculations if miss >5% (see term sheet).

Commercial proposal (summary):
- 12-month reserved commit: 30k GPU-hours/month.
- Discount: 22% off on-host list rate for the committed baseline. Additional 3% discount applied if signed within 15 days of proposal.
- SLA credit: 10% monthly credit for sustained under-delivery per the shortfall math in the term sheet.

Next steps:
- If this looks acceptable we can send a DocuSign for the term sheet and schedule an acceptance-run planning call. Proposed time: Tue 04/06 10:00am PT (45m) to review the harness and walk their infra team through the runner.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call to answer questions.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
